summary: A full request pool delays valid small demand restores and can exhaust a stricter client deadline without issuing their GET.
scenario: Cold daemon, s3_concurrency=16, sixteen real S3 GET bodies for valid ~32 MiB cache packs held after their first KiB; a distinct tiny pack request with deadline_ms=1000 returns found=false with zero wire GETs. With fifteen occupied slots the same kind of pack hits. Uniform 3000 ms caller hits after 2255 ms in the corrected control.

evidence.point: Each demand request acquires one pool permit; acquisition is bounded by the demand deadline and failures return a miss.
Entry packs call get_into, not buffered get.
Only buffered get acquires DownloadMemory; get_into streams through read_into without that reservation.
3/4 and 15/16 occupied controls hit; 4/4 and 16/16 occupied cases miss at 1000-1002 ms without GET.
Default-budget caller hits with one wire GET after 2255 ms.

trace: Rust wrapper send_remote_check -> socket RemoteCheck dispatch -> handle_remote_check_started_at -> handle_remote_check_leader -> demand GET queue -> V3Remote.download_entry -> RemoteLayout.get_into -> OpenDalBackend.read_into -> temporary disk file -> verified extraction/import, or deadline miss before GET.

authority.source: Issue #327 measurement request and production resource/backpressure failure mode
authority.quote: Measure that before building weighted permits.

severity: Cache reuse and compile latency under concurrent cold remote demand; no data loss, integrity failure, OOM or indefinite starvation demonstrated. A 1 s client/30 s daemon budget mismatch is supported production input, while uniform default clients had a successful delayed hit.
limits: Feature/scheduling measurement, not an admitted correctness defect. Endpoint holds tails deliberately; exact timings include an unsignalled 750 ms warming grace and overlap with another agent thin-LTO link.

summary: Three queue-only demand timeouts open the shared read breaker and suppress new valid reads after every occupied request permit has been released.
scenario: Pool=4, four valid ~1 MiB demand bodies are held. Three distinct valid tiny callers with 1 s budgets time out without wire GETs. Abort all held demands, await cancellation, and query public stats: total=4, used=0. A direct endpoint HEAD succeeds, but a new fourth valid tiny demand returns false after its warming grace with zero GETs. One-free-slot control serves all three callers and the recovery caller.

evidence.point: An error while waiting for the local semaphore calls breaker_permit.failure(classify_remote_error(error)).
Default read breaker threshold is 3; cooldown is 45 seconds.
Third classified failure opens the direction breaker until its cooldown deadline.
An open demand read breaker suppresses the request and returns a miss.
Matching green control, three overload misses, CAPACITY total=4 used=0, and recovery false with zero wire GETs; desired recovery assertion fails.

trace: Full local semaphore -> three typed deadline errors in demand GET queue -> shared read-direction failure count reaches 3 -> breaker Open(45 s) -> held requests cancelled and permits released -> later valid request rejected before backend dispatch.

authority.source: Production resource-saturation measurement requested in issue #327
authority.quote: whether that budget leaves a real saturation case

severity: A transient local saturation episode can suppress cache reuse across distinct subsequent read keys for the default 45 s cooldown. Execution proves immediate post-release suppression; 45 s duration is a pinned source constant, not an elapsed-time experiment. Writes have an independent breaker.
limits: This is explicit timeout/breaker policy and a measured scheduling amplification. No binding current promise forbids it, so it is not admitted as defect/gap. Changing that policy or giving small work priority is a feature/design decision.

summary: Do not infer unbounded memory growth, indefinite starvation, or a currently violated weighted-permit contract from issue #327.
checked: Pinned source demand budgets, request admission, streaming versus buffered paths, default prefetch reservation, existing memory/cancellation tests, one-free-slot controls, uniform default caller, and current issue body/comment.

closed_by.citation: investigation/evidence/baseline-controls.json; src/daemon.rs:43-67,2231-2242; src/remote_backend/download_memory.rs:34-48; issue #327 remains a measured-feature request. Default caller hit rather than starving indefinitely; memory tests prove accounting release within their tested seam.

reopens_if: A workload demonstrates a leak/unbounded allocation, a caller waiting beyond its enforced deadline, speculation exceeding its gate, or an approved fairness/SLO contract is supplied. Pool=1 has no speculative reserve by explicit source policy and was not load-tested here.

summary: Reject the initial default-client >=2500 ms experimental timing oracle.
checked: Initial probe measured a successful valid default-budget hit in 2256 ms but failed its drafted >=2500 ms assertion. Source shows 750 ms warming grace is consumed before initial bodies and later tiny requests; timing expectation was too strict. Corrected probe asserts observable default hit plus exactly one tiny wire GET and passes.
reopens_if: A supported default-budget small caller actually loses its valid cache hit under a reproducible workload and a binding contract makes that result wrongful.
